title: Netanyahu Announces Libel Suit Against Haaretz Over UAE Pre-Oct. 7 Warning Report
detail: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said Wednesday, September 9, 2026 that he has instructed his legal team to file a defamation lawsuit against Haaretz and reporter Shlomi Eldar over the previous day's report that United Arab Emirates President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan warned him roughly 10 days before October 7, 2023 that Hamas was preparing a major operation. Netanyahu's office called the report a 'malicious fabrication' and said reviews by the Prime Minister's Office, National Security Council and military secretariat found no record of any conversation between Netanyahu and Bin Zayed 'from the beginning of September through October 7, 2023.' Haaretz said it stood by its report, noting three senior foreign-government representatives were said to have been informed about the call at the time. The UAE Foreign Ministry reiterated that it 'does not comment on media stories or speculation regarding conversations between government leaders.' The dispute intensified as the year's third October 7 anniversary approaches: Haaretz's elections desk wrote Wednesday that the more Netanyahu 'tries to run from October 7, the more his culpability becomes a key election issue,' with the October 27 vote increasingly framed around the unresolved question of what he knew beforehand and why no state commission of inquiry has been established nearly three years on.

title: Haaretz: Hamas Offered to Release All Civilian Hostages Hours After Oct. 7 Attack; Blinken Calls Report 'Complete Fiction'
detail: As part of the same September 8, 2026 investigation (citing the forthcoming book 'Kidnapped: 843 Days of Abandonment' by Shlomi Eldar and Ruti Yuval) that revealed the disputed UAE pre-attack warning, Haaretz reported that on the evening of October 7, 2023 — hours after the attack began — Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani told then-Mossad chief David Barnea that Hamas was willing to immediately release all the civilian hostages it had seized, with no conditions attached, and offered Doha's mediation. According to Haaretz, Barnea rebuffed the offer, saying: 'If they want to release the civilians, let them release them ... We are not prepared to speak with Hamas.' Al Thani then called then-US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to say Israel was 'not interested' in Qatar's proposal; Haaretz reported Blinken responded 'Let's wait,' said he would speak with Netanyahu personally, and suggested waiting three days. Blinken rejected the account on X on Wednesday, September 9, 2026, writing: 'For the record, this is false. Complete fiction.' The Prime Minister's Office did not directly address the hostage-offer claim in its response to the broader Haaretz investigation, which it has called an 'absolute lie' over the separate UAE-warning allegation now the subject of Netanyahu's libel suit against Haaretz.
confidenceReason: The hostage-offer account is single-sourced to the same Haaretz book excerpt as the UAE-warning story; Blinken has publicly and specifically denied it as 'complete fiction,' while the Qatari and Israeli sides involved (Al Thani, Barnea) have not independently confirmed or denied their quoted exchange.
